lines.trans: Let us put the small wooden table right here under the tree, away from the door.
Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs instead of the lobby window.
Here is a clean white cloth and two blue teacups.
Mateo, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?
The wire needed straightening anyway. Nothing sentimental about good maintenance.
Oh, listen to Mr Maintenance! Yesterday you fixed the boiler, today you fix two brothers!
I fix pipes and chairs. People have to fix their own words.
What time does your watch say now, Mateo?
Eleven twenty. Cake ready, Rocio?
Cooling on the rack right now—golden crust and sweet lemon sugar!
Look upstairs at the attic window: Javier has changed his shirt three times!
Go talk to him, Clara, before he wears out the floorboards!

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Diminutive of la mesa.

examples.text: La mesita está aquí.
examples.trans: The small table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesitas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the small tables from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La madera está aquí.
examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Plural los árboles.

examples.text: El árbol está aquí.
examples.trans: The tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los árboles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trees from the door.

lejos.gloss: far; far away (lejos de = away from)

meanings.en: far; far away (lejos de = away from)
meanings.note: Opposite of cerca.

examples.text: La estación no está lejos.
examples.trans: The station is not far.

examples.text: Pon la mesa lejos de la puerta.
examples.trans: Put the table away from the door.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsula favourite for 'place' or 'seat'.

examples.text: El sitio está aquí.
examples.trans: The place is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sitios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the place from the door.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Wooden or folding chair.

examples.text: La silla está aquí.
examples.trans: The chair is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the chairs from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza firme.
examples.trans: It is a firm piece.

examples.text: Ahí suena la campana de la entrada. Un toque firme.
examples.trans: There goes the gate bell. One firm ring.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.text: La planta está aquí.
examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

meanings.note: Plantas aromáticas means culinary garden herbs.

examples.text: Es una pieza aromática.
examples.trans: It is an aromatic piece.

examples.text: Buen sitio. Dos sillas firmes, mirando a las plantas aromáticas en vez de a la ventana.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs instead of the lobby window.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: La vez está aquí.
examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.text: La ventana está aquí.
examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Plural los manteles.

examples.text: El mantel está aquí.
examples.trans: The tablecloth is here.

examples.text: Vemos los manteles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tablecloths from the door.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.text: Es una pieza blanca.
examples.trans: It is a white piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.text: La taza está aquí.
examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: El té está aquí.
examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

colgar.gloss: to hang; to hang up (the phone)

meanings.en: to hang; to hang up (the phone)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuelgo) and g -> gu in preterite 1st sg (colgué).

examples.text: Cuelgo el abrigo detrás de la puerta.
examples.trans: I hang my coat behind the door.

examples.text: Colgó los farolillos entre las ramas.
examples.trans: He hung the lanterns among the branches.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Plural faroles; classic wrought-iron courtyard lantern.

examples.text: Encendemos los faroles del patio al caer la tarde.
examples.trans: We light the courtyard lanterns at dusk.

examples.text: El farol de hierro alumbra toda la escalera.
examples.trans: The iron lantern lights up the whole staircase.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells z -> c: enderecé.

examples.text: Enderezo el cuadro de la pared.
examples.trans: I straighten the picture on the wall.

examples.text: El dueño se enderezó la corbata azul.
examples.trans: The owner straightened his blue tie.

meanings.note: Metal wire used for hanging lanterns or repairs.

examples.text: El alambre está aquí.
examples.trans: The wire is here.

examples.text: Vemos los alambres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wires from the door.

meanings.note: Polite reply meaning 'likewise / same to you', or 'anyway'.

examples.text: —¡Buen fin de semana! —¡Igualmente!
examples.trans: 'Have a nice weekend!' 'Likewise!'

examples.text: Sabía quién era y vino igualmente.
examples.trans: He knew who it was and came anyway.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Plural sentimentales.

examples.text: Ese reloj de bolsillo tiene un enorme valor sentimental para toda la familia.
examples.trans: That pocket watch has tremendous sentimental value for the whole family.

examples.text: Había que enderezar el alambre igualmente; nada sentimental, solo buen mantenimiento.
examples.trans: The wire needed straightening anyway—nothing sentimental, just good maintenance.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Building maintenance and repairs.

examples.text: El mantenimiento es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The maintenance is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mantenimiento.
examples.trans: We talk about the maintenance.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.text: ¿Me oyes bien por teléfono?
examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.text: El señor está aquí.
examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs naturally with preterite tense.

examples.text: Ayer arreglamos la caldera.
examples.trans: Yesterday we fixed the boiler.

examples.text: Llegué a Valencia ayer por la tarde.
examples.trans: I arrived in Valencia yesterday afternoon.

arreglar.gloss: to fix; to repair; to tidy

meanings.en: to fix; to repair; to tidy
meanings.note: Everyday verb for repairing things or sorting out problems.

examples.text: El vecino arregla la lámpara del salón.
examples.trans: El vecino fixes the lounge lamp.

examples.text: Ayer arreglamos la puerta del jardín.
examples.trans: Yesterday we repaired the garden gate.

meanings.note: Heating and hot-water boiler.

examples.text: La caldera está aquí.
examples.trans: The boiler is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boilers from the door.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.text: Hoy es viernes por fin.
examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.

examples.text: ¿Qué desayunamos hoy?
examples.trans: What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.text: El hermano está aquí.
examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.

examples.text: Soy yo, abre por favor.
examples.trans: It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Water or heating pipe.

examples.text: La tubería está aquí.
examples.trans: The pipe is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tuberías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipes from the door.

meanings.note: Always feminine (una persona amable) regardless of who it refers to.

examples.text: La persona está aquí.
examples.trans: The person is here.

examples.text: Vemos las personas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the persons from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Mi propia maleta = my own suitcase.

examples.text: Es una pieza propia.
examples.trans: It is an own piece.

examples.text: ¿Y no pidió su propia maleta con el tren de madera?
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: ¿Qué hora es? asks the clock time.

examples.text: La hora está aquí.
examples.trans: The hour is here.

examples.text: Vemos las horas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hours from the door.

marcar.gloss: to show (the time); to dial; to mark

meanings.en: to show (the time); to dial; to mark
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: marqué.

examples.text: El reloj de la torre marca las doce.
examples.trans: The tower clock shows twelve.

examples.text: Marqué el número de la estación.
examples.trans: I dialled the station number.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está tu caja de herramientas?
examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Covers wristwatches, wall clocks, and church tower clocks (plural: relojes).

examples.text: El reloj está aquí.
examples.trans: The watch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los relojes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the watchs from the door.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Las once = eleven o'clock.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte de la mañana.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty in the morning.

examples.text: Quedan once sillas limpias.
examples.trans: Eleven clean chairs remain.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Mide exactamente veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty.

meanings.note: Tall, light home-baked cake popular for breakfast or afternoon merienda in Spain.

examples.text: El bizcocho está aquí.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bizcochos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sponge cakes from the door.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.

examples.text: Es una arquitecta muy lista.
examples.trans: She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Takes an accent in present boot forms: se enfría.

examples.text: El bizcocho se enfría en la rejilla.
examples.trans: The cake cools on the wire rack.

examples.text: Bebe el té antes de que se enfríe.
examples.trans: Drink your tea before it gets cold.

meanings.note: Wire rack for cooling baked cakes.

examples.text: La rejilla está aquí.
examples.trans: The cooling rack is here.

examples.text: Vemos las rejillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cooling racks from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Golden crust of bread or cake, or tree bark.

examples.text: La corteza está aquí.
examples.trans: The crust is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cortezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the crusts from the door.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.text: Es una pieza dorada.
examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el azúcar.
examples.trans: We talk about the sugar.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; los dulces = sweets/pastries.

examples.text: Es una pieza dulce.
examples.trans: It is a sweet piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Top-floor room with sloping roof beams.

examples.text: La buhardilla está aquí.
examples.trans: The attic room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las buhardillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the attic rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.text: Cambio las toallas cada mañana.
examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.

examples.text: Cambiamos la mesa de sitio.
examples.trans: We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Buttoned shirt.

examples.text: La camisa está aquí.
examples.trans: The shirt is here.

examples.text: Vemos las camisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shirts from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Accented él ('he/him') is distinct from unaccented article el ('the').

examples.text: Él trabaja en el ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: He works at City Hall.

examples.text: Sube a hablar con él un minuto.
examples.trans: Go upstairs and talk to him for a minute.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

desgastar.gloss: to wear out; to wear down

meanings.en: to wear out; to wear down
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El paso del tiempo desgasta la piedra.
examples.trans: The passage of time wears down the stone.

examples.text: Tanto caminar desgastó las suelas.
examples.trans: Walking so much wore thin the soles.

meanings.note: Tablas de madera = wooden planks.

examples.text: La tabla está aquí.
examples.trans: The plank is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tablas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the planks from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

soler.gloss: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)

meanings.en: to usually do; to tend to (soler + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suelo, suele, suelen) used in present/imperfect + infinitive.

examples.text: Suelo tomar café a las ocho.
examples.trans: I usually have coffee at eight.

examples.text: Estos muros suelen guardar el fresco.
examples.trans: These walls usually keep the air cool.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!
